parts.problem_md:
Serial data transmission is used to transmit the data packets across the network.

**Explain **why serial data transmission is used to transmit the data packets.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of why serial data transmission is used include:

Any **three **of the following:

- The network may be spread over a long distance** ****[1 mark]**
- … so it is more reliable **[1 mark]**
- Bits will be sent/arrive in sequence **[1 mark]**
- … so bits less likely to be skewed **[1 mark]**
- Less crosstalk/interference **[1 mark]**
- … so less likely to have errors **[1 mark]**
- The data may not need to be transmitted at a fast speed **OR** data transmission speed of serial is adequate **[1 mark]**
- The cables in the network only use serial transmission **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A student has a sound file that is too large to be stored on their external secondary storage device. The student compresses the sound file to make the file size smaller.

The student sends the sound file to a friend. The file is transmitted across a network that uses packet switching.

**Explain **how the file is transmitted using packet switching.
parts.solution_md:
The file is transmitted using packet switching by:

Any **five **from:

- Data is broken/split/divided into packets **[1 mark]**
- Each packet (could) take a different route **[1 mark]**
- A router controls the route/path a packet takes **[1 mark]**
- … selecting the shortest/fastest available route/path **[1 mark]**
- Packets may arrive out of order **[1 mark]**
- Once the last packet has arrived, packets are reordered**[1 mark]**
- If a packet is missing/corrupted, it is requested again **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - An example of a 5 mark response could be:
> 
> *Packet switching is a method used to send data, like a sound file, over a network by breaking the file into smaller pieces called packets. Each packet can take a different route through the network, with routers deciding the quickest path for each one. Since the packets travel independently, they might arrive at the destination in a different order. Once all the packets arrive, the receiving computer reorders them using the information in the packets. If any packet is missing or corrupted, the system will request it again, ensuring that the entire file is received correctly.*

parts.problem_md:
The website hosts videos that users can stream. The company uploads new videos to the website.

The company uses parallel half-duplex data transmission to transmit the data for the new videos to the web server.

**Explain **why parallel half-duplex data transmission is the most appropriate method.
parts.solution_md:
Parallel half-duplex data transmission is the most appropriate method because:

Any **four **from:

- parallel would allow the fastest transmission  **[1 mark]**
- … of the large amount of data  **[1 mark]**
- data can be uploaded and downloaded  **[1 mark]**
- … but this does not have to be at the same time  **[1 mark]**
- data is not required to travel a long distance  **[1 mark]**
- … therefore skewing is not a problem  **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A company has a website that is stored on a web server.

The website data is broken down into packets to be transmitted to a user.

**Describe **the structure of a data packet.
parts.solution_md:
The structure of a data packet is described as:

Any **four **from the following:

- it has a header **[1 mark]**
- …that contains the destination address **[1 mark]**
- …that contains the packet number **[1 mark]**
- …that contains the originator’s address **[1 mark]**
- it has a payload **[1 mark]**
- it has a trailer **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - An example of a 4 mark answer could be:
> 
> *A data packet has a specific structure made up of three parts: the header, the payload, and the trailer. The header contains important information such as the destination address, the originator’s address, and the packet number. The payload is the actual data being transmitted, like part of a website. The trailer marks the end of the packet and ensures that the data has been received correctly*

parts.problem_md:
A student has a sound file that is too large to be stored on their external secondary storage device. The student compresses the sound file to make the file size smaller.

The compression method used reduces the sample rate and the sample resolution of the sound file.

The student sends the sound file to a friend. The file is transmitted across a network that uses packet switching.

**Identify **two pieces of data that would be included in the header of each packet.
parts.solution_md:
Two pieces of data that would be included in the header of each packet are:

Any **two **from:

- Destination/receivers (IP) address **[1 mark]**
- Packet number  **[1 mark]**
- Originator’s/senders (IP) address  **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Julia inputs personal data into her computer.

She stores three copies of the data using a hard disk drive (HDD), a solid state drive (SSD) and a USB flash memory drive.

Julia uses a USB connection to transfer data onto her USB flash memory drive

One benefit of using a USB connection is that it is a universal connection.

**State two **other benefits of using a USB connection.
parts.solution_md:
Example of benefits of using a USB connection are:

Any **two** from the following:

- It cannot be inserted incorrectly** [1 mark] **
- Supports different transmission speeds** [1 mark] **
- High-speed** transmission**** [1 mark] **
- **Automatically **detected (not connected)  **OR** automatically downloads drivers** [1 mark] **
- Powers the device (for data transfer)** [1 mark] **
- Backward compatible** [1 mark] **

> **[exam-tip]**
> Give benefits of the USB connection itself, not invented generic advantages like cost, storage capacity, security or durability
> 
> USB is a wired connection, so avoid describing it as wireless or citing serial transmission points such as data skew or long-distance range
